summary: THE ATMOSFERA is a no-code Earth observation project by solo participant Nik Alif Zaquan bin Nik Arzahar from Kedah, Malaysia, Team THE ATMOSFERA, Kuala Lumpur Virtual Hub, for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Challenge: Be An Earth System Trend Detective. Kuala Lumpur faces floods and heat. THE ATMOSFERA detects atmospheric trends using NASA open data. We used NASA Worldview to capture real satellite image of Kuala Lumpur at 3.1610, 101.6908, on 15 December 2024, during a major flood event. This is our original proof, uploaded to GitHub. We also used GPM IMERG for rainfall, Landsat for urban change, and MODIS for cloud cover. Our prototype is THE ATMOSFERA Gold dashboard, targeting Gold 135 to 150 marks across 10 criteria, with real NASA data proof section. This solution can help protect over 2 million people in KL, and in the future, support atmospheric monitoring for Moon habitats. From Kedah's paddy fields to the Moon. GitHub: github.com/AlifZaquan08/THE---AMOSTFERA. Email: alifzaquan1608@gmail.com.
details:
THE ATMOSFERA: The Next Frontier Shield is a no-code Earth observation project by solo participant Nik Alif Zaquan bin Nik arzahar from Kedah, Malaysia, Team THE ATMOSFERA, Kuala Lumpur Virtual Hub.

What does it do? It detects atmospheric and climate trends over Kuala Lumpur using NASA open Earth data. It monitors flood and heat risks.

How does it work? We used NASA Worldview to capture a real satellite image of Kuala Lumpur at 3.1610, 101.6908, on 15 December 2024, during a major flood event. We used GPM IMERG for rainfall, Landsat for urban change, and MODIS for cloud cover. Our Gold dashboard shows 10 criteria, 135 to 150 marks, with a real NASA data proof section.

What are the benefits? It can help protect over 2 million people in KL with early warning for floods and heat. It is no-code, so students in Kedah can use it easily.

What is the intended impact? To protect Earth today, and in the future, to support atmospheric monitoring for Moon habitats. From Kedah's paddy fields to the Moon.

What tools did we use? NASA Worldview, NASA Open Data Portal data. nasa.gov, api. nasa.gov, code. nasa.gov, GitHub for code and proof, Google Drive for videos and document, and AI builder for Gold dashboard design. No coding needed.

How is it creative? We combined Kedah local knowledge with NASA satellite data, and designed a Gold dashboard that is simple, visual, and scalable to any city and to the Moon.

What factors did we consider? Accuracy of NASA data, accessibility for non-coders, scalability, and real-world impact for KL floods
